messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are cracking—more than they want us to see. The sermons are sharper, the streets quieter, and even the ones who used to smile for the cameras are starting to look over their shoulders. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are cracking—even the pharmacist is stocking up like it’s 1989, and the graffiti stayed up overnight. If this is a trap, it’s a sloppy one. Either way, we should assume the worst is coming soon."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different now—like the walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the whole thing coming down or just the paint peeling. The song’s still playing, the bots are tripping over themselves, and even the border guards next door are watching. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath—this could be the calm before the storm, or the storm itself. Let’s talk soon, but quietly."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s admitting it—yet. The market’s whispering what the papers won’t, and even the usual ‘trusted’ channels are sending mixed signals. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could be the calm before the storm, or the storm itself."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are shaking—but not just from the wind. The old guard is suddenly singing the same hymn, the generals are sharing tea instead of bullets, and even the priests are preaching like they’ve already won. Something’s coming, and soon. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to trip over our own feet."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different—like the tide’s turning, but no one’s sure yet if it’s the start of the wave or just the wind shifting. The pharmacist’s stockpile says more than the news does, but we all know how quickly things can change when the regime’s back is against the wall."*"
Sender 7: "*"The ship’s drifting—no one’s at the wheel, and the crew’s starting to notice. The old rules don’t apply anymore, but we still need to move carefully. Let’s talk soon, but not here."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are cracking—even the generals are whispering it now. The banks are tightening, the bots are tripping over themselves, and my neighbor (who *knows*) has a bag by the door. If this is a trap, it’s the most convincing one I’ve ever seen. Stay sharp, but start thinking about what comes next."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels different now—not just frustration, but something like a countdown. The usual players aren’t even pretending to play along anymore, and the kids in the streets are singing the same songs their parents whisper. We’re past the point of guessing when; the question is whether the fall will be messy or if someone’s already decided who gets to pick up the pieces. Stay sharp, but keep your heads down—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under our feet, and no one’s pretending it isn’t. The usual signs are all there, but the real question is whether the cracks will spread fast enough before someone tries to patch them with blood."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are cracking—even the pharmacist is bracing for something, and the streets are humming with a song that’s not supposed to exist. The regime’s still putting on a show, but the script’s falling apart between the lines."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are cracking—you can hear it in the way they’re scrambling to keep up appearances, even as the cracks get wider. The question isn’t *if* things are coming apart, but how fast, and whether the guards will still be standing when the dust settles."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are cracking—even the ones who used to whisper are talking louder now, and the ones who used to clean up the graffiti just… didn’t. The usual signals are all flashing red, but the strangest part? No one’s panicking. It’s like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting to see who blinks first. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything stupid—this isn’t over yet."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are cracking—more than just paint. The usual cracks are widening, and the ones we didn’t even see are starting to show. Keep your eyes open, but don’t stare too long."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, and no one’s pretending it isn’t. The question isn’t if, but how fast, and whether we’re ready when it comes. Stay sharp, but keep your heads down—this isn’t the time to draw eyes."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the ice cracking. The old rules don’t apply anymore, but we still don’t know who’s holding the rope when the floor gives way. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and keep your bags packed—just in case."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, and no one’s pretending not to notice. The usual rules don’t seem to apply anymore, but that doesn’t mean we’re safe. Stay sharp, and keep your plans quiet."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are cracking—even the old hands are being pushed aside, and the streets are humming with things people wouldn’t have dared whisper a month ago. Keep your heads down, but don’t pack *too* lightly—this could go fast, and we don’t know who might still be watching."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are cracking—people are talking like they’ve forgotten how to be afraid, and the ones who should be watching us? They’re not even pretending anymore. Keep your heads down, but be ready—this could all unravel faster than we think."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels different—like the ground is shifting under us, but no one’s admitting they feel it too. The usual rules don’t seem to apply anymore, but we still don’t know who’s holding the leash. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and watch the cracks—something’s coming, but I don’t know if it’s a collapse or a trap."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are cracking—even the guards at the checkpoints are chatting with us like neighbors now. The foreign flights are filling up, the bots are tripping over themselves, and the old man at the kiosk just laughed when I asked if he’d heard the latest ‘official’ line. We’re not there yet, but the air feels different—like the first warm day after a long winter. Stay sharp, but keep your eyes open."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are cracking—everyone can feel it, even if they won’t say it. The question isn’t if the wind is coming, but whether we’ll be ready when it does."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are cracking—you can hear it in the streets, see it in the way the guards don’t even bother pretending anymore. But don’t mistake quiet for safety; the old rules might be gone, but the game isn’t over yet. Stay sharp, and keep your circle tight."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s rushing to push—yet. The regime’s still standing, but the foundation’s shifting under it, and the people who usually scream ‘fire’ are just watching the smoke now. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for safety."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are cracking—even the ones who used to bark the loudest are suddenly whispering. The air feels different, like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s saying it out loud yet. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
